title: Homestay Google Business Profile: Get Found on Maps
excerpt: A practical checklist to set up and verify a homestay Google Business Profile so you show up on Maps when travellers search "homestay near" your area.
description: Set up a homestay Google Business Profile that shows on Maps: verification, category, pin, photos, amenities, reviews and consistent contact details.
html:
To appear when travellers search "homestay near" a place, a homestay needs a verified Google Business Profile with the right primary category, an exact address and map pin, real photos, complete amenities, steady reviews with replies, and the same name, address and phone number everywhere online. Proximity matters too, so describe the places nearby accurately.

How homestays show up on Google Maps

When someone in Bengaluru types "homestay near Chikmagalur" or "homestay in Munnar with view", Google shows a map with a few properties before any website. Google says local results are based mainly on three things: relevance (how well your profile matches the search), distance (how far you are from the place searched), and prominence (how well known you are, including reviews and mentions across the web). You cannot change your distance, but you control almost everything about relevance and a good part of prominence.

For a family-run property, this is often the most valuable free listing you have. Guests who find you on Maps can call or message you directly, which supports the approach in our guide to B&B direct bookings without a booking engine.

Claim and verify the profile properly

Search for your property on Google Maps first. A profile may already exist, created by a guest or by Google from OTA data. If it does, claim it instead of creating a second one; duplicates split your reviews and confuse Google.

  • Use a Google account the business owns, not a staff member's personal account, and add a second family member as an owner or manager.
  • Google offers different verification methods depending on the business, such as a phone call, email or a short video showing the property, its signboard and proof you manage it. Follow the option your profile shows.
  • For a video, record continuously: the road or landmark, the signboard with the property name, the entrance, and something only staff can access, such as the reception desk or a key cabinet.
  • Put a visible signboard up before you verify. A property with no sign is harder to verify and harder for guests to find at night.

Google's help page on improving your local ranking explains the ranking factors, and the same help centre lists current verification steps.

Get the basics exactly right

Name

Use the real name on your signboard and registration. Adding keywords such as "Best Homestay Coorg Coffee Estate" to the name breaks Google's guidelines and can get a profile suspended. If your real name is "Hill View Homestay", that is fine as it is.

Primary category

The primary category is one of the strongest relevance signals. Start typing in the category field and choose the closest match for how you actually operate: for example, a lodging category such as guest house, bed and breakfast, farmstay or cottage. Pick what describes the stay, not what you hope ranks. Add secondary categories only if they are true.

Map pin and address

Rural addresses in Wayanad, Sikkim or Himachal are often vague. Drag the pin to your actual gate, not the village centre, and write the address the way a taxi driver would understand it, including the nearest landmark. A wrong pin sends guests down the wrong road and earns bad reviews.

Phone, hours and links

Use one primary phone number that is answered, ideally the same as your WhatsApp Business number. Add your website and enable messaging or WhatsApp if your profile offers it.

Photos and amenities that answer guest questions

Guests decide from photos. Upload your own, and keep adding them through the year so the profile looks alive.

Photo setWhat to include
ExteriorThe building in daylight, the gate and signboard, parking
RoomsEach room type, wide shot plus bathroom, in natural light
Common areasSit-out, dining area, garden, bonfire spot
FoodBreakfast spread and one or two signature home dishes
Views and surroundingsThe view from the property, the estate, the walk to the stream
HostsThe family, if they are comfortable, since that is what makes a homestay different

Then fill in every amenity Google lets you set for lodging: Wi-Fi, parking, breakfast, pet policy, hot water, kitchen access and so on. Each one is a fact Google can match to a search like "pet friendly homestay Ooty". Only mark what is true; a wrong amenity leads to a disappointed guest and a poor review.

Reviews: ask, reply and keep them coming

Reviews feed prominence and are what guests read most. A steady flow of recent reviews looks better than a burst from two years ago.

  • Create your review link from the profile dashboard and save it as a WhatsApp quick reply.
  • Ask in person at checkout, then send the link the next day with a short thank-you.
  • Never offer discounts or gifts in exchange for reviews, and never post reviews yourself or ask family to. Google removes fake reviews and can restrict profiles.
  • Reply to every review within a few days. Thank people by name, mention something specific, and keep replies to negative reviews calm and factual.
  • If a guest mentions a nearby place, such as "close to Abbey Falls", that helps future guests searching for it.

Updates, questions and keeping the profile active

Where your profile allows updates or posts, use them for practical news: monsoon access, a new room, a festival weekend, the coffee harvest. Google has changed which features lodging profiles get several times, so work with what your dashboard shows rather than what an old guide says.

If your profile shows a questions section, answer the common questions there yourself: check-in time, distance from the nearest town, whether cars reach the door, whether children are welcome. Check it monthly so a stranger's wrong answer does not sit there unanswered.

Keep your name, address and phone consistent everywhere

Google cross-checks your details across the web. Inconsistent listings weaken prominence and confuse guests. Make one master record and copy it exactly to:

  • Your website footer and contact page.
  • Airbnb, Booking.com, MakeMyTrip, Goibibo and Agoda listings, where the platform shows them.
  • Instagram and Facebook bios.
  • Your state tourism department's homestay listing, if you are registered.
  • Local directories and any tourism or district websites that list stays.

If you change your phone number, update all of them the same week.

Frequently asked questions

Why does my homestay not show up for "homestay near" searches?

Common reasons are an unverified or duplicate profile, a primary category that does not match lodging, a map pin in the wrong place, very few reviews, or simply distance from the place searched. Fix the basics first, then build reviews steadily. Proximity cannot be changed, so also make sure your website mentions the nearby towns and attractions you genuinely serve.

Can I add keywords like "best homestay" to my business name?

No. Google's guidelines ask for your real business name as it appears on your signboard and documents. Adding keywords can lead to a suspended profile, and competitors can report it. Put descriptive words in your business description, photos and website instead. A clean, real name also looks more trustworthy to guests comparing several properties.

How many photos should a homestay upload?

There is no magic number. Aim to cover every room type, the bathrooms, the common areas, food, views and the approach road, so a guest can picture the whole stay. Then add a few new photos every month or season. Recent, honest photos matter more than a large number of old or heavily edited ones.

Should I reply to every Google review?

Yes, ideally within a few days. Replies show future guests that a real host is paying attention, and they give you a chance to correct misunderstandings calmly. Keep replies short and personal. For negative reviews, acknowledge the issue, explain what you changed, and invite the guest to contact you directly rather than arguing in public.

Where to start

Search for your property on Google Maps today and claim or create the profile. Fix the name, primary category, pin and phone number, then upload a full set of room and property photos. After that, save your review link as a quick reply and ask every departing guest.
